perspective:
I’m Jose Castillo. I’m a heavy equipment operator and I sometimes help with maintenance and repairs at the community bank where Patricia Ndiaye works as a teller. We have a friendly, professional relationship and usually chat about everyday things.

Recently, I noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn and less vibrant than usual. When I asked if she was okay, she said it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked me for asking. I told her I was there if she ever wanted to talk or needed someone to listen. She said that meant a lot.

During a lunch break, I overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments. I brought up financial planning strategies I’d been reading about and offered to discuss them. She said that could be helpful and that she’d been overwhelmed with her bills lately. I suggested we could look over budgeting tips together whenever she felt up to it, and she said she’d take me up on that soon.

Afterward, I worried I might have overstepped by bringing up her finances. I told Patricia I only wanted to help, not pry. She said she didn’t think I was prying and that she was grateful for the offer. I said I respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend. She said it was good to know she had someone to turn to.

Later, I checked in with her by asking about her weekend plans. She said she was doing fine and planned a quiet weekend at home, but she didn’t share more. I got the sense she appreciated my concern but preferred to handle things privately, so I kept the support low-key and made sure she knew I was available.

Since then, I’ve continued to check in with her at work. She’s said she’s busy but handling it, thanked me for checking in, and told me it’s really great to have my support. I’ve told her she can let me know if she needs anything, even just grabbing a coffee, and that we’re all there to help each other out.
final_response:
From Jose’s perspective, I first noticed Patricia seemed upset. Then I learned she was worried about bills and financial commitments, so I believed she had financial difficulties. After offering help, I worried I might have overstepped and that she could misconstrue my advice. Later, I sensed she appreciated my concern but valued her privacy. Finally, her continued thanks and saying my support meant a lot showed me that my supportive presence was beneficial.

ANSWER: b
